backlog.title: External Transport & Firmware Layer
backlog.description: Typed-command support in the qmk_notifier Rust crate (v0.3.0) and typed-command dispatch in the qmk-notifier firmware. These are prerequisite external-repo changes that unblock QMKonnect's host-side rules feature. The crate gains new RunCommand variants, CommandResponse, and multi-report typed framing; the firmware gains the 0xF0 discriminator, handle_typed_command dispatcher, and the QUERY_INFO/QUERY_CALLBACK/SET_OS/APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT handlers that use the already-scaffolded host_layer/host_cb_enabled/has_been_queried state.

milestones.title: qmk_notifier Crate v0.3.0 — Typed-Command Transport
milestones.description: Add typed-command RunCommand variants, HostOs enum, CommandResponse enum, typed-command framing (0x81 0x9F 0xF0 prefix, multi-report chunking), response parsing (0x51 typed vs 0/1 legacy vs timeout), and change run() to return CommandResponse. Tag release v0.3.0.

tasks.title: Typed-Command Framing (multi-report chunking with 0xF0 discriminator)
tasks.description: Frame typed commands using [0x81, 0x9F, 0xF0, cmd_id, args...] with the same ETX-framed, multi-report chunking as strings. APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT may span reports (uncapped callback-id list).

subtasks.title: Implement typed-command payload builder and multi-report framing
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The crate's send_raw_report() (src/core.rs:~80) builds a 33-byte buffer per report: [0x00, 0x81, 0x9F, <30 payload bytes>]. The existing framing appends ETX (0x03) before chunking in run() (lib.rs:~200). batches_for(data) = (data.len() + 29) / 30. The device cache (LazyLock<Mutex<Option<DeviceCache>>>) and burst_to_one() are reusable as-is. Typed commands must use the SAME multi-report path because APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT can carry >30 bytes of callback ids.
2. INPUT: RunCommand variants from P1.M1.T1.S1, CommandResponse from P1.M1.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: Add a function `fn build_typed_payload(cmd: &RunCommand) -> Vec<u8>` in core.rs that serializes a typed command into raw bytes: prefix [0x81, 0x9F, 0xF0, cmd_id], then command-specific args (QUERY_INFO: none; QUERY_CALLBACK: [index]; SET_OS: [os_byte]; APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT: [layer, flags, count, id...]), then ETX (0x03). The layer byte for APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT is the layer number or 0xFF for clear. flags bit 0 = clear_board. This payload is then chunked via the EXISTING batches_for/burst_to_one path (the [0x00] report-ID byte and the [0x81, 0x9F] header are already in the buffer layout, so the typed path writes [0x81, 0x9F, 0xF0, cmd_id, args..., ETX] as the payload AFTER stripping the existing header — or restructure to build the full payload including header). CRITICAL: the existing send_raw_report prepends [0x00, 0x81, 0x9F] in burst_to_one's buffer; for typed commands the third byte becomes 0xF0. The cleanest approach is to pass the full payload (starting with 0xF0, cmd_id, args) to send_raw_report, which already prepends [0x00, 0x81, 0x9F].
4. OUTPUT: A function that produces the wire payload for any RunCommand variant, for consumption by P1.M1.T2.S2.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on build_typed_payload. No external doc files changed.

subtasks.title: Wire typed commands into run() dispatch and send path
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: run() in lib.rs:~190 currently matches on RunCommand::SendMessage (append ETX, call send_raw_report) and RunCommand::ListDevices (call list_hid_devices). The new typed variants must route through send_raw_report with their typed payload from P1.M1.T2.S1.
2. INPUT: build_typed_payload() from P1.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: Extend run()'s match arms: for QueryInfo/QueryCallback/SetOs/ApplyHostContext, call build_typed_payload(cmd) to get the payload bytes, then call send_raw_report(payload, vid, pid, page, usage, verbose). The send_raw_report function already handles device cache lookup, burst-write, and IN-drain. After the burst, the IN-drain currently discards replies — P1.M1.T3.S1 will modify burst_to_one to optionally return the first IN report instead of draining all.
4. OUTPUT: Extended run() that dispatches all RunCommand variants, for consumption by P1.M1.T3.S1 (response parsing).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on the new match arms. No external doc files changed.

tasks.title: Response Parsing & run() Return Type Change
tasks.description: Parse the 32-byte IN report after a typed burst into CommandResponse. Change run() to return Result<CommandResponse, QmkError>.

subtasks.title: Implement response reader and parser (0x51 typed vs 0/1 legacy vs timeout)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: burst_to_one() in core.rs:~200 currently drains IN reports with read_timeout(0) in a bounded loop (IN_DRAIN_MAX=32), discarding them. For typed commands, we need to READ the first IN report (with a short timeout, e.g. 100ms) and parse it. response[0]==0x51 ⇒ typed (decode by cmd_echo at response[1]); response[0] in {0,1} ⇒ Legacy{matched}; no reply within timeout ⇒ Timeout. HidReadError and NoResponseReceived error variants already exist in error.rs. For QUERY_INFO response: [0x51, 0x01, proto_ver, feature_flags, callback_count, board_rules_present(0/1)]. For QUERY_CALLBACK: [0x51, 0x02, index, name_bytes...NUL-padded]. For SET_OS/APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT: [0x51, cmd_echo, ack(0/1)].
2. INPUT: RunCommand variant being sent (from P1.M1.T2.S2 dispatch), the device handle from the cache.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add a new function `fn read_typed_response(device: &HidDevice, expected_cmd: u8, verbose: bool) -> Result<CommandResponse, QmkError>` that reads one 32-byte IN report with a 100ms timeout. On Ok(n>0): check response[0]==0x51 and response[1]==expected_cmd, then decode per the command table. On Ok(0) or timeout: return CommandResponse::Timeout (not an error — the caller decides what to do). (b) Modify burst_to_one to optionally return the first IN report instead of draining all. Alternatively, add a separate `burst_and_read_one()` function for typed commands that writes all reports then reads exactly one response. The existing burst_to_one continues to drain-discard for the SendMessage path (backward compat).
4. OUTPUT: CommandResponse for consumption by the caller (run()), which returns it. Downstream qmkonnect handshake (P4.M2.T1.S1) pattern-matches on Info/Ack/Timeout.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on read_typed_response and the response format. No external doc files changed.

subtasks.title: Change run() signature to return CommandResponse and wire response parsing
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: run() currently returns Result<(), QmkError>. This is a BREAKING API change: qmkonnect's QmkNotifier::notify (src/core/notifier.rs:142-186) currently does `qmk_notifier::run(params)` and discards the result with Ok(_). After this change, the return is CommandResponse. The SendMessage path returns CommandResponse::Legacy{matched: bool} (parsed from the legacy 0/1 response), and ListDevices returns CommandResponse::Legacy{matched: false} (or a new variant). Typed paths return their parsed CommandResponse.
2. INPUT: read_typed_response from P1.M1.T3.S1, the existing send paths from P1.M1.T2.S2.
3. LOGIC: Change `pub fn run(params: RunParameters) -> Result<(), QmkError>` to `pub fn run(params: RunParameters) -> Result<CommandResponse, QmkError>`. For SendMessage: after send_raw_report succeeds, read one IN report (the legacy 0/1 reply) and return CommandResponse::Legacy{matched: response[0]==1}. For typed commands: call the typed send + read_typed_response, return the parsed CommandResponse. For ListDevices: return CommandResponse::Legacy{matched: false} (or a no-op variant).
4. OUTPUT: Updated run() returning CommandResponse. This is the final crate API surface for v0.3.0.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the crate README.md to document the new return type and CommandResponse variants.

milestones.title: qmk-notifier Firmware — Typed-Command Dispatch
milestones.description: Add the 0xF0 discriminator check, handle_typed_command() dispatcher, and QUERY_INFO/QUERY_CALLBACK/SET_OS/APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT handlers. The state variables (host_layer, host_cb_enabled, has_been_queried) and callback registry are already scaffolded.

tasks.title: Typed-Command Dispatch Infrastructure
tasks.description: Add the 0xF0 discriminator check at the top of hid_notify() and implement the handle_typed_command() dispatcher.

subtasks.title: Add 0xF0 discriminator check and handle_typed_command() skeleton in hid_notify()
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: notifier.c hid_notify() (lines 543-577) currently checks data[0]==0x81 && data[1]==0x9F, strips the 2-byte header, then processes legacy bytes. The 0xF0 discriminator must be checked AFTER stripping the 2-byte header: if data[0]==0xF0 (which is now the first byte after stripping), route to handle_typed_command(). The constants NOTIFY_CMD_DISCRIMINATOR=0xF0, NOTIFY_CMD_QUERY_INFO=0x01, etc. are already defined in notifier.h. The host state variables (host_layer, host_cb_enabled, has_been_queried) are already declared at notifier.c:137-139.
2. INPUT: None (the constants and state are already defined in notifier.h and notifier.c).
3. LOGIC: In hid_notify(), after `data += 2; length -= 2;`, add: `if (length >= 1 && data[0] == NOTIFY_CMD_DISCRIMINATOR) { handle_typed_command(data + 1, length - 1); return; }`. Implement `static void handle_typed_command(uint8_t *data, uint8_t length)` that switches on data[0] (cmd_id) to QUERY_INFO(0x01), QUERY_CALLBACK(0x02), SET_OS(0x03), APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT(0x05). Each handler builds a 32-byte response and calls raw_hid_send. has_been_queried is set to true on the first QUERY_INFO.
4. OUTPUT: The dispatch skeleton for consumption by P1.M2.T2.S1-S4 (individual handlers).
5. DOCS: none — firmware C code has no user-facing doc surface.

subtasks.title: Implement set_host_layer() and apply_host_callbacks() helper functions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: notifier.c:137-138 declares `static uint8_t host_layer = LAYER_UNSET;` and `static bool host_cb_enabled[HOST_CALLBACK_MAX] = {false};`. The board-layer equivalents are activate_layer()/deactivate_layer() (notifier.c:~225-240). LAYER_UNSET=255 and HOST_LAYER_BASE=224 are defined. layer_on()/layer_off() are QMK functions. get_host_callbacks()/_size() return the registry (weak defaults {NULL,0}).
2. INPUT: handle_typed_command skeleton from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement `static void set_host_layer(uint8_t layer)`: if layer==0xFF, layer_off(host_layer) and set host_layer=LAYER_UNSET. Else if host_layer != LAYER_UNSET, layer_off(host_layer). Then layer_on(layer) and host_layer=layer. This operates ONLY on the host tracker, never touching board activated_layer. Implement `static void apply_host_callbacks(const uint8_t *ids, uint8_t count)`: for each id in 0..HOST_CALLBACK_MAX, if id was in host_cb_enabled but NOT in the new ids set, call the callback's on_disable and clear the flag. Then for each id in the new set, if NOT already enabled, call on_enable and set the flag. This is the disable-before-enable diff. Guard against NULL on_enable/on_disable and ids >= HOST_CALLBACK_MAX.
4. OUTPUT: Two helper functions consumed by APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT handler (P1.M2.T2.S4).
5. DOCS: none — firmware C code.

tasks.title: Typed-Command Handlers (QUERY_INFO, QUERY_CALLBACK, SET_OS, APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT)
tasks.description: Implement the four typed-command response builders and the APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT clear_board logic.

subtasks.title: QUERY_INFO handler: proto_ver, feature_flags, callback_count, board_rules_present
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: board_rules_present() (notifier.c:193) already exists and checks all default + per-OS maps. get_host_callbacks_size() returns the callback count (weak default 0). NOTIFY_PROTO_VER=2, NOTIFY_FEATURE_APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT=0x01, NOTIFY_FEATURE_CALLBACK_REGISTRY=0x02 are in notifier.h. NOTIFY_RESPONSE_MARKER=0x51.
2. INPUT: handle_typed_command dispatcher from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: On QUERY_INFO (0x01): set has_been_queried=true. Build response[32]={0}: response[0]=0x51 (NOTIFY_RESPONSE_MARKER), response[1]=NOTIFY_CMD_QUERY_INFO (0x01), response[2]=NOTIFY_PROTO_VER (2), response[3]=feature_flags (0x01 if board_rules_present() or always, bitwise-OR 0x02 if get_host_callbacks_size()>0), response[4]=get_host_callbacks_size() (as u8), response[5]=board_rules_present() ? 1 : 0. Call raw_hid_send(response, RAW_REPORT_SIZE).
4. OUTPUT: 32-byte QUERY_INFO response for the host's handshake (consumed by qmkonnect P4.M2.T1.S1).
5. DOCS: none — firmware C code.

subtasks.title: QUERY_CALLBACK handler: return callback name by index
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: host_callback_t has fields { name: const char*, on_enable: callback_t, on_disable: callback_t }. get_host_callbacks() returns the array, get_host_callbacks_size() the count. Names are C strings (NUL-terminated). Response format: [0x51, 0x02, index, name_bytes..., 0x00 padding].
2. INPUT: handle_typed_command dispatcher from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: On QUERY_CALLBACK (0x02): read the index from data[1]. If index >= get_host_callbacks_size(), respond with [0x51, 0x02, index, 0x00] (name = NULL/empty). Else, get the callback at that index, copy its name string into response[3..] (NUL-padded to fill 32 bytes). response[0]=0x51, response[1]=0x02, response[2]=index. Call raw_hid_send(response, RAW_REPORT_SIZE).
4. OUTPUT: 32-byte QUERY_CALLBACK response for the host's name sweep (consumed by qmkonnect P4.M2.T1.S1).
5. DOCS: none — firmware C code.

subtasks.title: SET_OS handler: update current_os
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: current_os (os_variant_t) is declared at notifier.c:132. notifier_set_os() (notifier.c:~480) handles OS changes with idempotent guard + state clear. For typed SET_OS, we can call notifier_set_os() directly with the os_byte mapped to os_variant_t. os_variant_t mapping: 0=OS_UNSURE, 1=OS_LINUX, 2=OS_WINDOWS, 3=OS_MACOS, 4=OS_IOS.
2. INPUT: handle_typed_command dispatcher from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: On SET_OS (0x03): read os_byte from data[1]. Call notifier_set_os((os_variant_t)os_byte). Build response [0x51, 0x03, 0x01] (ack=ok). raw_hid_send(response, RAW_REPORT_SIZE).
4. OUTPUT: SET_OS ack for the host (consumed by qmkonnect P4.M2.T1.S1).
5. DOCS: none — firmware C code.

subtasks.title: APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT handler: clear_board, set_host_layer, apply_host_callbacks
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: set_host_layer() and apply_host_callbacks() from P1.M2.T1.S2. The board equivalents are deactivate_layer() and disable_command() (notifier.c:~225-260). The clear_board flag (data bit 0) tells the firmware to clear board state before applying host context. Request format after discriminator+cmd_id: [layer][flags][count][id...]. layer=0xFF means clear host layer. Multi-report: the full message is reassembled in hid_notify's msg_buffer before dispatch — but wait, typed commands are NOT reassembled through msg_buffer (they bypass the ETX reassembly). REVISE: typed commands MUST be ETX-framed and multi-report reassembled, same as strings. The handle_typed_command must reassemble the full typed payload across reports before parsing. This means the 0xF0 check should happen AFTER ETX reassembly, not per-report. See HOST_RULES.md §5: 'Framing: ETX-framed and multi-report like strings.'
2. INPUT: set_host_layer() and apply_host_callbacks() from P1.M2.T1.S2, QUERY_INFO from P1.M2.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: REVISED approach — the 0xF0 discriminator check must happen AFTER ETX reassembly, inside process_full_message or just before it. In hid_notify(), after ETX triggers msg_buffer dispatch, check if msg_buffer[0]==0xF0 before calling process_full_message. If 0xF0: route to handle_typed_command(msg_buffer, msg_index) which parses the full reassembled payload: cmd_id=msg_buffer[1], then command-specific args. For APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT (0x05): layer=msg_buffer[2], flags=msg_buffer[3], count=msg_buffer[4], ids=&msg_buffer[5..5+count]. If flags bit 0 (clear_board): deactivate_layer() + disable_command() (clear board state first). Then set_host_layer(layer). Then apply_host_callbacks(ids, count). Build response [0x51, 0x05, 0x01] (ack). raw_hid_send(response, RAW_REPORT_SIZE).
4. OUTPUT: APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT ack for the host (consumed by qmkonnect P4.M3.T1.S1).
5. DOCS: none — firmware C code.

backlog.title: QMKonnect Pattern Matcher — Full-Parity Port
backlog.description: Port the firmware pattern_match.c Thompson-NFA matcher to Rust at src/core/pattern.rs. This is a full-parity port (not a subset) including *, ^, $, WT(), +, and all character classes (\d \D \w \W \s \S \b \B .). All constructs are linear-time in the NFA. The port is the foundation for host-side rule evaluation and must produce identical results to the firmware matcher for every pattern/string pair.

milestones.title: Pattern Matcher Port (src/core/pattern.rs)
milestones.description: Create the new src/core/pattern.rs module, register it in src/core/mod.rs, and port the complete firmware matcher with parity tests against the firmware test corpus.

tasks.title: Escape Processing & Pattern Parsing
tasks.description: Port process_escapes() (escape sequences, dot, + quantifier placeholder bytes) and parse_pattern() (anchor detection, core extraction, even-backslash-count rule).

subtasks.title: Port process_escapes() to Rust — escape/class/quantifier byte transform
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The firmware process_escapes() (pattern_match.c:15-75) transforms a pattern string into processed bytes: \x01-\x04 = escaped literals ^$*\, \x05-\x0A = classes \d\D\w\W\s\S, \x0B-\x0C = assertions \b\B, \x0D = dot, \x0E = + quantifier marker, 0x2A = glob * (wildcard). Literal . and + (when not after a consumable element) are emitted as ordinary ASCII 0x2E/0x2B. The `last_consumable` flag tracks whether the previous element consumed a char (determines whether + is quantifier or literal). See architecture/external_deps.md §3 for the full byte contract.
2. INPUT: None (greenfield module).
3. LOGIC: Create src/core/pattern.rs. Implement `fn process_escapes(pattern: &str) -> Vec<u8>` that mirrors the C function exactly. Track `last_consumable: bool`. For each byte: if backslash + next char, emit the appropriate placeholder byte. If bare *, emit 0x2A and set last_consumable=false. If bare + after consumable, emit 0x0E and set last_consumable=false; if + after non-consumable, emit literal 0x2B. If bare ., emit 0x0D. Otherwise emit the byte literally. Register the module in src/core/mod.rs with `pub mod pattern;`.
4. OUTPUT: process_escapes() function for consumption by P2.M1.T1.S2 (parse_pattern).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add rustdoc on process_escapes explaining the placeholder byte contract. No external docs changed yet.

subtasks.title: Port parse_pattern() — anchor detection and core extraction
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The firmware parse_pattern() (pattern_match.c:~100-160) detects a leading ^ (start_anchored), a trailing $ with an EVEN backslash count (end_anchored — the even-backslash-count rule is critical: abc$=anchor, abc\\$=escaped, abc\\\\$=anchor), carves out the core between anchors, and calls process_escapes on the core. The parsed_pattern_t struct holds { core_pattern, start_anchored, end_anchored, processed_pattern }.
2. INPUT: process_escapes() from P2.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement `struct ParsedPattern { core: Vec<u8>, start_anchored: bool, end_anchored: bool }` and `fn parse_pattern(pattern: &str) -> ParsedPattern`. Detect leading ^ → start_anchored=true, advance past it. For trailing $: walk left from end-1 counting consecutive backslashes; if even count, end_anchored=true, truncate. Extract core substring between anchors, call process_escapes() on it. Handle empty core (^$ matches empty string).
4. OUTPUT: ParsedPattern for consumption by P2.M1.T2.S1 (NFA matching).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on parse_pattern explaining the even-backslash-count rule.

tasks.title: Thompson NFA Engine (compile, simulate, match)
tasks.description: Port the Thompson NFA construction, epsilon-closure, and two-list simulation. This is the core matching engine guaranteeing O(states × input_len) without backtracking.

subtasks.title: Port NFA compiler (nfa_compile) and state types
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The firmware nfa_compile() (pattern_match.c:~350-430) builds a State pool via Thompson construction. Opcodes: OP_CHAR (consume one matching byte), OP_ANY (consume any byte incl newline — glob *), OP_SPLIT (epsilon fork for * and +), OP_ASSERT (zero-width \b/\B), OP_MATCH (accepting). X+ compiles to exactly 2 states (OP_CHAR + OP_SPLIT loop-back). Glob * compiles to OP_SPLIT→OP_ANY(loop-back)→exit. The `tail` pointer threads the dangling exit slots. The pool is stack-allocated fresh each call with lastlist zeroed.
2. INPUT: ParsedPattern from P2.M1.T1.S2 (the processed core bytes).
3. LOGIC: Define `enum NfaOp { Char(u8), Any, Split(usize, usize), Assert(u8), Match }` (using indices instead of pointers for Rust safety). Implement `fn nfa_compile(pat: &[u8]) -> Vec<NfaOp>` that walks the processed bytes and builds the state list. For 0x2A (glob *): emit Split + Any(loop-back). For 0x0B/0x0C: emit Assert. For 0x0E after a consuming element: convert the previous Char/Any into Char+Split loop-back. For other consuming bytes: emit Char. Append Match at the end. Use a Vec<NfaOp> and index-based edges (no raw pointers).
4. OUTPUT: Compiled NFA (Vec<NfaOp>) for consumption by P2.M1.T2.S2.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc referencing Russ Cox's paper and explaining linear-time guarantee.

subtasks.title: Port epsilon-closure (nfa_addstate) and NFA simulation (nfa_match)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The firmware nfa_addstate() (pattern_match.c:~460-500) follows epsilon transitions (OP_SPLIT forks and conditional OP_ASSERT edges) with a `lastlist` generation guard that prevents infinite recursion. nfa_match() (pattern_match.c:~520-570) is a two-list simulation: maintain clist (current live states) and nlist (next live states), bump nfa_gen once per phase for O(1) dedup, feed one input char per step, check for OP_MATCH in the list. The full_match flag controls prefix/substring vs consume-whole-string. is_word_boundary(str, pos) checks XOR of neighboring word-char-ness.
2. INPUT: Compiled NFA from P2.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: In Rust, use a `generation: usize` counter and a `Vec<bool>` seen-set (indexed by state index) instead of the C lastlist field. Implement `fn nfa_addstate(states: &[NfaOp], idx: usize, list: &mut Vec<usize>, seen: &mut Vec<bool>, generation: usize, string_start: &[u8], abspos: usize)`. For Split: recurse both branches. For Assert: check is_word_boundary, recurse if condition holds. For Char/Any/Match: add to list. Implement `fn nfa_match(pattern: &[u8], str_bytes: &[u8], case_sensitive: bool, full_match: bool) -> bool` using two Vec<usize> lists swapped per step. Port is_word_boundary, is_digit_char, is_word_char, is_whitespace_char, pattern_char_matches from the C originals. The empty-string special case for \b/\B: if string is empty, neither boundary nor non-boundary passes.
4. OUTPUT: The core nfa_match function for consumption by P2.M1.T3.S1 (anchor strategy).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on nfa_match explaining the two-list simulation.

tasks.title: Public API, Anchor Strategy & Delimiter-Aware Matcher
tasks.description: Port match_with_anchors() (anchor strategy), the public pattern_match() entry point, and the delimiter-aware match_pattern() from notifier.c.

subtasks.title: Port match_with_anchors() and public pattern_match() entry
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: match_with_anchors() (pattern_match.c:~170-200) selects the NFA mode based on anchor flags: ^...$ exact → one full match from offset 0; ^ prefix → one reach-any from offset 0; $ suffix → loop offsets, full match from each; substring → loop offsets, reach-any from each (empty core only matches empty string). The public pattern_match(pattern, str, case_sensitive) calls parse_pattern → match_with_anchors → free.
2. INPUT: nfa_match from P2.M1.T2.S2, ParsedPattern from P2.M1.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: Implement `fn match_with_anchors(parsed: &ParsedPattern, s: &str, case_sensitive: bool) -> bool` with the four anchor modes. Implement `pub fn pattern_match(pattern: &str, s: &str, case_sensitive: bool) -> bool` as the public entry. Each mode calls nfa_match with full_match=true (exact/suffix) or full_match=false (prefix/substring). For substring mode: loop str.char_indices() and call nfa_match from each offset.
4. OUTPUT: Public pattern_match function for consumption by P2.M1.T3.S2 (delimiter matcher) and downstream by rules.rs.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on pattern_match documenting all supported constructs (*, ^, $, +, \d, etc.).

subtasks.title: Port delimiter-aware match_pattern() and Pattern enum (Single/Parts)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: match_pattern() (notifier.c:~290-340) handles the GS delimiter (0x1D): if pattern has GS but message doesn't, match pattern_left against whole message; if message has GS but pattern doesn't, match pattern against msg_left (class only); if both have GS, split both and match both halves; neither has GS, direct match. HOST_RULES.md §8(2) defines Pattern::Single(String) and Pattern::Parts(String, String) for rules.toml.
2. INPUT: pattern_match from P2.M1.T3.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement `pub enum Pattern { Single(String), Parts(String, String) }` with serde Deserialize (untagged — string → Single, array of 2 → Parts). Implement `pub fn match_pattern(pattern: &Pattern, app_class: &str, title: &str, case_sensitive: bool) -> bool` that mirrors the C match_pattern logic using GS (0x1D) as delimiter. For Single(p): if title is non-empty, match p against app_class only (firmware parity); else against whole string. For Parts(c, t): both halves must match.
4. OUTPUT: Pattern enum and match_pattern function for consumption by P3.M1.T2 (rules evaluation).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on Pattern and match_pattern with WT() examples.

tasks.title: Rule Evaluation — Layer/Callback Matching & Stack/Replace Decision
tasks.description: Implement the evaluate() function that takes a RuleSet and a window string, matches layer rules (first-match) and callback rules (all-match), resolves callback names to IDs, and determines stack vs replace.

subtasks.title: Implement evaluate() with layer first-match, callback all-match, and HostContext output
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: HOST_RULES.md §8(3) Per-window evaluation: (1) Layer: first matching layer_rule → L_h (else none). (2) Callbacks: ALL matching callback_rules → desired enabled callback id set; each rule's disable names are explicit exclusion (removed from desired set). (3) Stack-vs-replace: window is replace iff EVERY matched rule's effective disable_firmware_config is true. HOST_RULES.md §4: the host decides per window whether the board runs — send the string first iff the board has rules AND at least 1 matched rule is non-disabling. The match_pattern function from P2.M1.T3.S2 takes a Pattern, app_class, title, and case_sensitive.
2. INPUT: RuleSet from P3.M1.T1.S1, match_pattern from P2.M1.T3.S2, name_to_id: HashMap<String, u8> from the handshake (P4.M2.T1.S1 — for now accept as parameter).
3. LOGIC: Define `pub struct HostContext { pub layer: Option<u8>, pub callback_ids: Vec<u8>, pub clear_board: bool, pub any_match: bool }`. Implement `pub fn evaluate(rules: &RuleSet, app_class: &str, title: &str, name_to_id: &HashMap<String, u8>, board_has_rules: bool) -> HostContext`. Scan layer_rules in order; first match_pattern() success → layer = Some(rule.layer), record the rule's effective disable_firmware_config. Scan ALL callback_rules; for each match, add enable names (resolved via name_to_id) to the desired set, remove disable names. Collect effective disable_firmware_config from all matched rules. If no rules matched → HostContext { layer: None, callback_ids: vec![], clear_board: false, any_match: false }. If matched → clear_board = all matched rules have effective disable_firmware_config == true (AND board_has_rules is considered: string is sent iff board_has_rules AND NOT all-disabling).
4. OUTPUT: HostContext for consumption by P4.M3.T1.S1 (notify_qmk send logic).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on evaluate() and HostContext with the stack/replace decision rules.

tasks.title: Capability Handshake (QUERY_INFO, QUERY_CALLBACK sweep, SET_OS)
tasks.description: Implement the handshake that detects host-capable firmware, builds the name→id callback map, sends SET_OS, and sets the global capable flag.

subtasks.title: Implement handshake function and global capability state
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: HOST_RULES.md §8(5) specifies the handshake: run(QueryInfo) → if Info{proto_ver:2, flags&0x01} → run(SetOs(host_os)) → for i in 0..callback_count: run(QueryCallback(i)).name → name_to_id map → validate rules.toml names. Re-trigger only on device transition via is_device_connected() poll. The host determines its OS: Linux/Windows/macOS. startup_device_probe (notifier.rs:77-125) is called at startup by every runner. The Notifier trait's send_command (from P4.M1.T1.S1) is the path to send typed commands.
2. INPUT: send_command from P4.M1.T1.S1, DeviceFilter from configured_filter(), HostOs enum from the crate.
3. LOGIC: Add global state: `static HOST_CAPABLE: AtomicBool` (false), `static CALLBACK_NAMES: Lazy<Mutex<HashMap<String, u8>>>`. Implement `pub fn perform_handshake(verbose: bool)` that: (1) builds filter via configured_filter(), (2) calls send_command(QueryInfo, &filter), (3) matches on CommandResponse::Info{proto_ver:2, feature_flags, callback_count, ..} if flags & 0x01 → capable, (4) if capable: send SetOs based on cfg!(target_os), sweep callbacks via QueryCallback(i) for i in 0..callback_count, populate CALLBACK_NAMES, validate rules.toml callback names against the map (warn, don't fail), set HOST_CAPABLE=true. On Timeout/Legacy/non-v2: set HOST_CAPABLE=false (string-only). Deduplicate by tracking has_handshaked state (once per board boot).
4. OUTPUT: HOST_CAPABLE flag and CALLBACK_NAMES map for consumption by P4.M3.T1.S1 (send logic).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rustdoc on perform_handshake.

subtasks.title: Integrate handshake into startup and device-status poll
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Each runner (runners/{windows,macos,linux}.rs) calls startup_device_probe(verbose) at startup. The device-status poll threads (tray.rs ~312/379, linux_tray.rs ~76/254) call is_device_connected() on a background thread and emit transitions. The handshake should run after startup_device_probe if a device is found, and on false→true device transitions.
2. INPUT: perform_handshake from P4.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: In each runner's startup sequence, after startup_device_probe, call perform_handshake(verbose) if is_device_connected() returns true. In the device-status poll threads (tray.rs and linux_tray.rs), on a false→true transition, call perform_handshake(verbose) on the polling thread (non-blocking to the UI thread). Add a has_handshaked guard so the handshake runs at most once per board boot (reset on device disconnect).
4. OUTPUT: Handshake integrated into the startup/poll lifecycle for consumption by P4.M3.T1.S1.
5. DOCS: none — internal lifecycle integration.

tasks.title: Host-Context Send Logic (stack, replace, no-match clear)
tasks.description: After the debounced string send, evaluate rules and send the appropriate APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT command, or clear on no-match.

subtasks.title: Implement host-context evaluation and send in debounce worker
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The debounce_worker (notifier.rs:223-284) flushes pending by calling notifier.notify(message). After P4.M1.T2.S2, pending carries PendingMessage{payload, window_info}. HOST_RULES.md §8(4) specifies the send logic: Stack (board has rules AND at least 1 matched rule non-disabling): send string first, then APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT{layer, callbacks, clear_board=false}. Replace (all matched rules disabling, OR board has no rules): send ONLY APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT{layer, callbacks, clear_board=true}. No match: APPLY_HOST_CONTEXT{layer=0xFF, callbacks=empty}. The evaluate() function from P3.M1.T2.S1 produces HostContext. HOST_CAPABLE and CALLBACK_NAMES from P4.M2.T1.S1 gate the host-rules path.
2. INPUT: PendingMessage from P4.M1.T2.S2, evaluate() from P3.M1.T2.S1, HOST_CAPABLE and CALLBACK_NAMES from P4.M2.T1.S1, send_command from P4.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: In the debounce worker's flush step (and in the immediate-send path in notify_qmk): (1) If NOT HOST_CAPABLE OR no rules.toml: send the legacy string only (current behavior, unchanged). (2) If HOST_CAPABLE AND rules.toml present: call evaluate(rules, &window_info.app_class, &window_info.title, &CALLBACK_NAMES, board_has_rules). Then: if ctx.any_match AND NOT ctx.clear_board (stack mode): send the string first via notify(payload), then send_command(ApplyHostContext{layer: ctx.layer, callbacks: ctx.callback_ids, clear_board: false}). If ctx.any_match AND ctx.clear_board (replace mode): send ONLY send_command(ApplyHostContext{..., clear_board: true}). If NOT ctx.any_match: send_command(ApplyHostContext{layer: None, callbacks: vec![], clear_board: false}). Retry/cache parity with SendMessage (device errors swallowed after 3 retries per §5.4).
4. OUTPUT: Functional host-context send logic that completes the host-rules feature end-to-end.
5. DOCS: none — internal pipeline logic.
